analysis: The code snippet defines getInteger(String property) which retrieves a property value via this.getProperty(property). If the value is null, it returns -1. Otherwise, it attempts to parse the value as an integer using Integer.parseInt(v). The called function parseInt may throw java.lang.NumberFormatException when the input string is not a valid integer (e.g., empty string, non-digit characters, decimal points, whitespace). Since NumberFormatException is a runtime exception, it is not required to be caught, but the current code only handles the null case and does not handle invalid formats, causing the exception to propagate. To make the function robust, it is advisable to catch NumberFormatException within this snippet and return a default value (e.g., -1) similar to the null case. The only statement that can throw this runtime exception is 'return Integer.parseInt(v);'. Therefore, catching should occur around that statement.
